name: Little Traverse Bay Protection and Restoration Fund Grants
summary: Annual grants for projects in the Little Traverse Bay watershed in Michigan that control invasive species, manage stormwater and restore shoreline, following the watershed management plan. Nonprofits, agencies and schools can apply.

geography.label: Little Traverse Bay watershed, Emmet and Charlevoix counties, Michigan

eligibility.rule: A 501(c)(3) nonprofit, government agency or school serving the Little Traverse Bay watershed
Addresses one or more objectives in the current watershed management plan
Proposed work has not already occurred
Current tax status and, if applicable, Michigan charitable-solicitation registration
Does not discriminate in hiring or providing services

documents: Current operating budget with actuals to date, except schools or municipalities
Prior operating budget with year-end actuals, except schools or municipalities
List of the organization's board of directors

applicant_types.quote: 501(c)(3) nonprofits, government agencies, and schools serving the Little Traverse Bay watershed are eligible to apply for a grant.

geography.quote: While most of our grantmaking focuses exclusively on Emmet County, we recognize the Little Traverse Bay watershed extends into Charlevoix County as well.

access.quote: Interested organizations must first inquire before applying.

amount.quote: There is no minimum or maximum grant size, though most prior grants from this fund have been in the $10,000-$30,000 range.

window.quote: Grants are awarded annually to organizations that address specific objectives in our region's Little Traverse Bay Watershed Management Plan

effort.quote: Interested organizations must first inquire before applying.
You complete your grant application online; include your organization's current operating budget and last year's final budget; and a list of your organization's board of directors.
Step 4: We review your grant application.

eligibility.quote: 501(c)(3) nonprofits, government agencies, and schools serving the Little Traverse Bay watershed are eligible to apply for a grant.
An applicant's proposed work must address one or more objectives stated in the current Little Traverse Bay Watershed Management Plan.
Additionally, we do not reimburse activities that already occurred.
Applicants must be current with their tax status and, if applicable, their registration to solicit charitable donations in Michigan;
Organizations that do not discriminate in hiring of staff or the provision of services.

after_award.quote: If awarded a grant, the recipient has up to 20 months to complete the proposed work, after which a final report is due to the Community Foundation.

documents.quote: Organization's operating budget for its current fiscal year, with actuals to-date (not required for schools or municipalities).
Organization's operating budget for its prior fiscal year, with year-end actuals (not required for schools or municipalities).
List of your organization's board of directors
